diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment. The issue is likely due to the database connection pool being exhausted.
diagnosis.root_cause: The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the database connection pool size to 10, leading to connection pool exhaustion in production.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool settings and set max_connections to 10.
Staging p95 latency is 180 ms with no connection pool issues.
Staging connection pool stats show no signs of exhaustion.
All pods are running and healthy with version v4.17.
The migration to orders-client v3 is the likely cause of the connection pool configuration change.
Production p95 latency is consistently high at 2150 ms since the deployment.

ruled_out: The staging environment with the same version does not show latency issues, ruling out a code-level bug.
The deployment did not affect other services, ruling out a shared infrastructure issue.

proposal.rationale: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the deployment of version v4.17, likely due to the database connection pool being exhausted. The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the connection pool size to 10, which is insufficient for production demand. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, will restore the connection pool settings and resolve the issue. This action is supported by the runbook and aligns with the observed evidence.
